global.description: Global configuration applied across all rules in this document.

basePath.description: Prefix prepended to every REST path pattern before matching, e.g. "/api".

rateLimit.description: Default rate limit applied unless a rule declares its own `rateLimit` override. Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per window.

cors.description: Default CORS policy applied unless a rule declares its own `cors` override. Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package.

providers.description: Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package. Intended to dynamically grant authorities based on claims.

when.description: JavaScript expression evaluated against `claims`; truthy activates this provider.

authorities.description: Authorities granted to the caller when `when` evaluates truthily.

propertyNames.description: Path pattern in path-to-regexp syntax, e.g. "/users/:id".

authorities.description: Authority groups checked against the union of claims.authorities, claims.roles, and space-separated claims.scope tokens. Outer array is AND (every group must be satisfied), inner array is OR (at least one authority in the group must match). Omit, or use an empty/null value, to require only that the caller is authenticated. Example: [["ADMIN", "users:read"]] means ADMIN OR users:read; [["ADMIN"], ["users:read"]] means ADMIN AND users:read.

expression.description: Optional JavaScript expression check evaluated in addition to (and after) the authorities check.

value.description: JavaScript expression source evaluated at request time; must return a truthy value for the rule to allow the request. REST rules see `claims` and `req` (body, params, query, headers, cookies) in scope; GraphQL rules see `claims`, `args`, `source` (the resolver's parent/source value — useful for ownership checks like `source.id === claims.sub`), and `info` (the GraphQLResolveInfo). Example: "args.input.username.toLowerCase() !== 'admin'".

message.description: Custom error message surfaced when the expression returns falsy. Defaults to "Expression check failed".

authenticated.description: Declares that this route needs a signed-in caller and no particular authority. Documentary — every matched rule already requires one — but far clearer than an empty `authorities` list or an expression on `claims.sub`. Cannot be combined with `public: true`.

public.description: Lets anonymous callers reach this rule instead of being answered 401. Only for routes that carry their own credential (e.g. a share-link token the service validates). Cannot be combined with `authenticated: true`.

cors.description: Per-rule CORS override. Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package.

rateLimit.description: Per-rule rate-limit override. Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per window.

keto.description: Per-object permission checks answered by Keto, evaluated in order after `authorities` and `expression`. Each entry is one check with its own denial: list `view` (NOT_FOUND) then `edit` (FORBIDDEN) to get the 404-then-403 ladder. Requires the guard to be given a permission evaluator — a rule that asks for one without it throws rather than denying.

namespace.description: Keto namespace of the object, e.g. "Bookmark". Named here rather than in a URL, so no Keto address ever appears in a rules file.

permit.description: The relation the caller must hold on the object, e.g. "view" or "edit".

id.description: Where the object id is read from on the request: "param.<name>", "query.<name>" or "json.<path>" (dotted). Validated at startup. A path resolving to a LIST requires the permit on every element; a path resolving to nothing is a wiring mistake and throws — it is never an allow. Defaults to "param.id".

permissions.description: Permission requirement in disjunctive normal form: the OUTER list is OR, the INNER list is AND — [[A, B], [C]] reads "(A and B) or C". NOTE this is the OPPOSITE nesting to `authorities` above, which is outer-AND / inner-OR. It is deliberate: this is the same grammar as the `@check` directive and `ketoCheck()`, so one permission reads identically wherever it is declared. The two are not confusable in practice — an authority is a string, a permission term is an object.

onDeny.description: How a failure of THIS check is answered. NOT_FOUND (the default) is the same answer as for an id that never existed, so ids cannot be probed. FORBIDDEN is for a second check on an object the caller can already see.

message.description: The i18n key the denial carries, e.g. "bookmarks.errors.not-found". Defaults to "errors.not-found" / "errors.insufficient-permissions" — the same fallbacks as `ketoCheck()`, because two rails that refuse the same thing must say it with the same words.

It is deliberate: this is the same grammar as the `@check` directive and `ketoCheck()`, so one permission reads identically wherever it is declared. The two are not confusable in practice — an authority is a string, a permission term is an object.

onDeny.description: How a failure of THIS check is answered. NOT_FOUND (the default) is the same answer as for an id that never existed, so ids cannot be probed. FORBIDDEN is for a second check on an object the caller can already see.

message.description: The i18n key the denial carries, e.g. "bookmarks.errors.not-found". Defaults to "errors.not-found" / "errors.insufficient-permissions" — the same fallbacks as `ketoCheck()`, because two rails that refuse the same thing must say it with the same words.

authorities.description: Authority groups checked against the union of claims.authorities, claims.roles, and space-separated claims.scope tokens. Outer array is AND (every group must be satisfied), inner array is OR (at least one authority in the group must match). Omit, or use an empty/null value, to require only that the caller is authenticated. Example: [["ADMIN", "users:read"]] means ADMIN OR users:read; [["ADMIN"], ["users:read"]] means ADMIN AND users:read.

expression.description: Optional JavaScript expression check evaluated in addition to (and after) the authorities check.

value.description: JavaScript expression source evaluated at request time; must return a truthy value for the rule to allow the request. REST rules see `claims` and `req` (body, params, query, headers, cookies) in scope; GraphQL rules see `claims`, `args`, `source` (the resolver's parent/source value — useful for ownership checks like `source.id === claims.sub`), and `info` (the GraphQLResolveInfo). Example: "args.input.username.toLowerCase() !== 'admin'".

message.description: Custom error message surfaced when the expression returns falsy. Defaults to "Expression check failed".

authenticated.description: Declares that this route needs a signed-in caller and no particular authority. Documentary — every matched rule already requires one — but far clearer than an empty `authorities` list or an expression on `claims.sub`. Cannot be combined with `public: true`.

public.description: Lets anonymous callers reach this rule instead of being answered 401. Only for routes that carry their own credential (e.g. a share-link token the service validates). Cannot be combined with `authenticated: true`.

rateLimit.description: Per-rule rate-limit override. Reserved for future use — not currently enforced by the policy evaluators in this package.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per window.

keto.description: Per-object permission checks answered by Keto, evaluated in order after `authorities` and `expression`. Each entry is one check with its own denial: list `view` (NOT_FOUND) then `edit` (FORBIDDEN) to get the 404-then-403 ladder. Requires the guard to be given a permission evaluator — a rule that asks for one without it throws rather than denying.

namespace.description: Keto namespace of the object, e.g. "Bookmark". Named here rather than in a URL, so no Keto address ever appears in a rules file.

permit.description: The relation the caller must hold on the object, e.g. "view" or "edit".

id.description: Where the object id is read from on the request: "param.<name>", "query.<name>" or "json.<path>" (dotted). Validated at startup. A path resolving to a LIST requires the permit on every element; a path resolving to nothing is a wiring mistake and throws — it is never an allow. Defaults to "param.id".
